key_factors: Accelerating revenue growth: Q2 FY26 revenue +9.7% YoY, Q3 FY26 +12% YoY with record $15.84B
AI infrastructure orders raised to $9B for FY26 (from $5B), product orders +35% YoY
Strong EPS growth: +31% YoY in Q2, +37% YoY in Q3 (GAAP), with raised FY26 guidance to $62.8-63.0B revenue
Solid balance sheet: debt-to-equity 0.515, ROE improving to 23.2%, gross margin 64.8%
Valuation extremely stretched: P/E 41.6x at top of 12-month range (25.8-41.6), P/B 9.6x at peak, stock +54% in one quarter
Gross margin compression risk: non-GAAP gross margin fell to 66.0% from 68.6% due to memory costs and tariffs
Security segment flat YoY (~$2B), underperforming the broader portfolio acceleration
Near-term catalyst (Q3 beat + guidance raise) already priced in via +17% single-day move on May 14

sources_cited.excerpt: Cisco Systems reported stronger-than-expected Q3 results with revenue of $15.84 billion beating estimates and raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance. AI-related orders now expected to reach $9 billion (up from $5 billion). Product orders surged 35% year-over-year.

Revenue increased 12% in the quarter ended April 25, from $14.15 billion a year earlier. Net income rose to $3.37 billion, or 85 cents per share, from $2.49 billion, or 62 cents per share, a year earlier.

Adjusted gross margin slipped to 66.0 percent from 68.6 percent a year earlier, with management citing memory cost pressure and the estimated impact of current tariff policy. Security revenue at roughly $2 billion was flat year over year.
Cisco holds about 43 percent of global Ethernet switching revenue and nearly 60 percent of enterprise routing revenue as of 2025
